events.title: Certiorari Denied in Heath v. Florida
events.summary: The Supreme Court of the United States denied the application for a stay of execution and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Ronald P. Heath v. Florida, et al. The application was initially presented to Justice Thomas, who referred it to the full Court. The denial means that the execution of Ronald P. Heath's death sentence will proceed as scheduled, and the Court will not review the case.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari and stay of execution affects the administration of justice and the finality of death penalty cases.

events.title: Certiorari Denied in Simpson v. Quick
events.summary: The Supreme Court denied the application for a stay of execution and the petition for a writ of certiorari in the case of Kendrick Simpson v. Quick, Warden, et al. The application was initially presented to Justice Gorsuch, who referred it to the full Court. The denial means that the execution of Kendrick Simpson's death sentence will proceed as scheduled.
events.why_relevant: The denial of certiorari and stay of execution affects the administration of justice and the finality of capital punishment cases.
